![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14221452/assets/e933e484b931ee54b345a8e7af3b0e44f80a8b019e3e401007ad4987192e33be.png)

Find the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x = t^2 - 1, \qquad y = t^3 - 4t
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t \in [-2,0].$
current_example.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x = x(t), \qquad
y = y(t), \qquad
t_1 \leq t \leq t_2
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
\int_{t_1}^{t_2} y \dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{\textrm{d}t} \:\textrm{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1) \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}({t}^{3}-4t)(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{-2}^{0}{t}^{2}({t}^{2}-4)\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a negative number since $y\dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{\textrm{d}t} \leq 0$ for all $t \in [-2,0].$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =-2{\int }_{-2}^{0}{t}^{2}({t}^{2}-4)\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{-2}^{0}{t}^{2}(4-{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{-2}^{0}(4{t}^{2}-{t}^{4})\text{d}t \\  & =8{\int }_{-2}^{0}{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t-2{\int }_{-2}^{0}{t}^{4}\,\text{d}t \\  & =8\cdot \frac{{t}^{3}}{3}\,{|}_{-2}^{0}-2\cdot \frac{{t}^{5}}{5}\,{|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =8(\frac{{0}^{3}}{3}-\frac{(-2)^{3}}{3})-2(\frac{{0}^{5}}{5}-\frac{(-2)^{5}}{5}) \\  & =8(\frac{8}{3})-2(\frac{32}{5}) \\  & =\frac{64}{3}-\frac{64}{5} \\  & =\frac{128}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
